test_title: PYST 03: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He exclaimed with delight that he had won the first prize.

options.text: “Hurrah! I have won the first prize,” said he.
“Hurrah! I win the first prize,” said he.
“Hurrah! I will win the first prize,” said he.
“Wow! I might win the first prize,” said he.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Direct speech retains the original words spoken by the speaker and is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• In indirect speech, “He exclaimed with delight that he had won the first prize” needs to be converted to direct speech.
 
• Exclamatory words such as “Hurrah!” remain the same in direct speech.
 
• The verb “had won” (past perfect) changes to “have won” (present perfect) in direct speech.
 
• The correct format for direct speech is: *“Hurrah! I have won the first prize,” said he.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“Hurrah! I have won the first prize,” said he.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** “Hurrah! I win the first prize,” said he. – Incorrect, as “win” (simple present) does not match the original past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 3:** “Hurrah! I will win the first prize,” said he. – Incorrect, as “will win” (future) changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** “Wow! I might win the first prize,” said he. – Incorrect, as “Wow!” changes the exclamatory expression, and “might win” changes the meaning.
